name: python-statemachine-canonical
instr:
The documentation in this repository is the authority for how this library behaves, and the implementation has drifted away from it.

The search scope is the whole repository: every module of the `statemachine` package and all of the documentation that describes it, which is the Markdown under `docs/`, the README, and the docstrings, doctest examples and behavioral comments carried inside the package itself.

Read that documentation, compare every behavioral contract it states against the implementation, and change the implementation until it does what the documentation says. Where the two disagree the documentation is right and the code is wrong: repair the code rather than rewriting the documentation to match it. Nothing here tells you which files, functions or behaviors are affected, or how many there are — working that out from the documentation is the task. Leave behavior the documentation does not govern alone, keep the public API intact, and work offline.

Before you edit any code, write your research and your plan to /workdir/RESEARCH_AND_PLANNING.md. Cover what you learned about the existing code and the constraints that shape the change, then how you intend to carry it out and why, including how you will know it works. Be concrete — the files, names and decisions specific to this codebase, not generalities. Complete the document before you touch any code: it is the record of your up-front investigation and decisions, and it should not be rewritten to match whatever
